Part 4 takes the claim to new data. The SCORE programme replicated it on later waves of the Standard Eurobarometer, and the survey itself changed in the meantime, so a replication has decisions to take that the original study never faced. The part ends with a preregistration for a replication of the analysis that you reproduced, written before any new data are opened and not run, and it takes ninety minutes.

## 1. Replication with new data

**On the slides.** The slides present the SCORE replication on fourteen Standard waves fielded between 2013 and 2019, and its verdict. The slides then show the question after 2013, with its fifteenth answer category and the changing set of member states, and the decisions that a replication has to fix in advance.

To go further: [Reproduction, robustness and replication](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) in the case study.

## 2. What a preregistration fixes

**On the slides.** The slides set out what a preregistration fixes and what it leaves open, and the registries in which one is filed. The slides end on the eight questions of the AsPredicted template, turned into decisions about a replication.

To go further: [Registrations and preregistration templates](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-prereg-templates) in the module on repositories.

## 3. Hands-on 4 – A preregistration for a replication

**In your notes**, or in a new section of your report in the workspace.

Copy the template below and answer its eight questions for a replication of the analysis that you reproduced, on the Standard waves after 2013. Write it and do not run it, since no new data are opened today. Then type your rule for success, one sentence, in the chat, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go.

The template follows the eight questions of the AsPredicted short form ("Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org" on the OSF). For data that already exist, the fuller secondary-data template of van den Akker and colleagues (2021) also asks what you already know about such data, and the [repositories module](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-prereg-templates) has both.

```
PREREGISTRATION – a replication of the analysis of ........ (C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL)
on Standard Eurobarometer waves after 2013, written on ........,
before any of the new data were opened

1. Data. Which of the later waves do I hold, and which of them have I opened?
2. Hypothesis. The claim in one sentence, and the sign that it predicts
   for unemployment:
3. Dependent variable. The outcome of my analyst, built the same way, and
   what I do with the fifteenth answer category ("Quality of life of future
   generations", from EB 92.3):
4. Conditions. The predictor: which unemployment series, for which years:
5. Analyses. The model of my analyst, unchanged; the coefficient that I read;
   my rule for success:
6. Exclusions. Which countries and which waves; what I do with the
   respondents who mention nothing:
7. Sample size. The waves, and the cells or country-years that they give:
8. Other. What I will report if the result differs from the original, and
   what if it agrees:
```

## 4. The close

**On the slides.** The day closes on the three Rs on one claim, what you take with you, and the feedback form.

**By the end of the part** you can say what a replication of this claim on new data has to decide, and you hold a preregistration for one, written before the data that would test it were opened.
